data.name: Comanche 4
data.detailed_description:
The best-selling Comanche series returns with this fast-paced action game that places you at the controls of a Comanche RAH-66 helicopter. In 6 single player campaigns and multiplayer, the game combines serious firepower with effortless controls and stunning, interactive terrain.
Features
  • NON-STOP ASSAULT — Blast away at tanks, jets, aircraft carriers, helicopters, missile-launching troops and more.
  • UNLEASH THE POWER — Shoot Hellfire and Stinger missiles, rockets and a 20mm cannon.
  • AIRBORNE IN MINUTES — Quickly master flying and fighting using the keyboard & mouse, or for the sim fan, joystick, throttle & pedal controls.
  • STUNNING INTERACTIVE TERRAIN — Immerse yourself in detailed environments with rotor wash, shadows, terrain scarring and spectacular explosions.
  • 6 EXTREME CAMPAIGNS — Fly across urban, forest, arctic, desert and sea environments while you protect diplomats, support Delta Force, subdue renegade forces, attack warships and more.

reviews.review:
Comanche 4, developed by the same studio which released the Delta Force series, is a first-person or cockpit-view helicopter shooter with tactical, arcade and simulation elements, although mostly arcade-style playable. 

After about 6 hours play time in a completionist approach, here’s my pros / cons list:

Pros: 
+ same engine as Delta Force (DF) Land Warrior but with major graphic upgrades, like higher model detail, and especially a 1280x1024 resolution option which was the highest possible back then
+ easy controls
+ controls layout and functionality easy to learn and master
+ good mix of simulation and arcade elements
+ lots of missions
+ varied map landscapes
+ tactical approach somewhat possible
+ long-range view
+ running well on modern systems (played 2026)

Cons: 
-	despite the graphics improvements compared to DF titles, the engine still had an outdated flair already at the time of its release
-	missing save option during missions, despite DF having this feature included a year earlier
-	monotonous search, destroy, protect missions
-	missing a story
-	missions are only a series of flight assignments without connection
-	some concepts of DF games put in a helicopter simulator
-	sneaking / stealth approach practically impossible due to map design, enemy positioning and the latter being able to spot even just a millimetre of the player’s helicopter, sometimes through obstacles or landscape elements like trees
-	even on easy difficulty, most missions are pretty hard and require quite a few retries
-	a night mission would have been very interesting

Conclusion: 
Overall, a very repetitive game that does a good job at combining simulation and arcade elements in this helicopter shooter. It does have some engine-inherent game design and difficulty balancing issues though. Interesting probably only for flight simulator fans and those of the Comanche series for nostalgia. 

Rating: 4/10 points
